$comment: RESEARCH OUTPUTS.
What exists, where it is, and — where it is not public — who holds it.
WHAT THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONTAIN: a DOI, a journal name, a
conference, or a citation for anything that does not have one. Three theses
were written, examined and defended; none has been published in a journal,
and saying otherwise would be the exact failure mode this whole review was
about. `status` carries the honest answer instead, and the page prints it
next to every entry rather than burying it.
public     — anyone can open it right now, and `url` proves it
on-request — it exists, I hold it, ask me
internal   — belongs to the organisation named in `heldBy`, not mine to publish
planned    — intended, not yet done. Says so, so it cannot read as done.
tests/content.test.js fails the build if a `public` entry has no url, if a
url does not resolve, or if a non-public entry carries one anyway.
THE REPOSITORIES. Each entry with a github.com url says only what that
repository itself shows: no result its README states as a target, no
standard it maps to called 'compliance', and no client or partner it names.
`lenses` places an output with no case study of its own in a role view
(content/lenses.json ids); every lens must have at least one public piece
of work beyond this site's own pages, here or among its case studies'
artifacts (scripts/lib/content.js, checkLensWork).
intro: This page says which is which — because a portfolio that lists outputs without saying whether anyone can read them is a list of assertions.

outputs.title: A study of socioeconomic drivers of river export of multiple pollutants in sub-basins worldwide, and qualitative future storylines for African coastal water pollution
outputs.summary: Modelled multi-pollutant river export across 10,226 sub-basins with MARINA-Multi, identified the socioeconomic drivers statistically, and built qualitative scenario storylines for African coastal waters under climate change.
outputs.note: Examined and defended. Not deposited in a public repository — ask and I will send it.

outputs.title: Approach to soft path water management: thinking beyond cement, steel and pipes — Freetown as case study
outputs.summary: Argued that Freetown's water gap is not primarily a pipe-capacity problem, and developed demand-side, reuse and community-stewardship alternatives scoped for resource-constrained settings.
outputs.note: Defended May 2021, on a full Chinese Government (MOFCOM) scholarship.

outputs.title: Mapping groundwater potential in the Freetown Complex: a geophysical approach
outputs.summary: Electrical-resistivity surveying combined with geological and hydrogeological data into GIS potential maps for hard igneous rock, validated by subsequent drilling.
outputs.note: First class honours, graduated top of class. The method went on to inform real siting work.

outputs.title: Becoming a Boat: towards a flood-resilient Wuppertal
outputs.venue: Academic Consultancy Training, Wageningen University & Research
outputs.heldBy: Municipality of Wuppertal / Wageningen University & Research
outputs.summary: Flood-risk assessment for the city and its suspended railway, combining historical records, climate projections, GIS and stakeholder workshops into an implementation roadmap.
outputs.note: Delivered to the client; the report is theirs.

outputs.title: Inventory of 54 global hazard information systems
outputs.venue: UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
outputs.summary: Catalogued global hazard information systems, expanding the organisation's regional and hazard-type coverage, alongside a terminology standardisation for economic loss and damage reporting.
outputs.note: Contributed to UNDRR's internal databases in support of the Sendai Framework Monitor.

outputs.title: Risk-management factsheet — Trinidad and Tobago
outputs.venue: UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction
outputs.summary: National-level risk-management factsheet produced to inform policy, drawing on the audited Caribbean disaster-loss data.

outputs.title: Groundwater Investigation Toolkit
outputs.summary: Python and browser code for rural borehole projects in Sierra Leone: resistivity soundings, drilling logs, pumping tests and water quality in; figures, borehole designs and .docx reports out. The repo links a browser app.
outputs.note: A toolkit dated 2026, not the records of my 2018–2019 fieldwork. Its worked examples are partly illustrative or synthetic, as the repo says.

outputs.title: GAIA Framework 2.2 — Green AI Assessment
outputs.summary: An open (MIT) framework, Excel workbook and web estimator for the energy, carbon and water footprint of an organisation's AI use, with uncertainty tiers. It maps its outputs to disclosure lines in GRI, ESRS E1 and E3, IFRS S2, CDP and SBTi.
outputs.note: A mapping to disclosure line items, not a claim of compliance. Its estimator weighs workloads typed into it and cannot read actual usage.

outputs.title: climatematch-pipeline — climate extremes for West Africa
outputs.summary: A Python starter pipeline that pulls historical CMIP6 runs (1980–2014) and observed temperature and precipitation for West Africa, computes monthly-based extreme indices, fits GEV 20-year return levels and builds a graph of which models behave alike.
outputs.note: Built for the Climatematch Academy course. Historical runs only; code on GitHub, with no licence file.

outputs.title: GloBox A/B test analysis
outputs.summary: SQL queries and a Python notebook (t-tests, confidence intervals, power analysis) on whether a new banner on GloBox's mobile website paid off, from a Masterschool data-analytics sprint. The README links a Tableau Public dashboard.
outputs.note: Coursework. Conversion rose with the banner and spending did not, so the advice was to hold off.

outputs.title: Sustainable AI Prototypes
outputs.summary: Browser prototypes that make generative AI's energy and carbon use visible: a prompt coach and dashboard, a department display, a Tetris-style usage visual, a digital forest and a Chrome extension (v1.0). A November 2025 team project, revised after partner feedback.
outputs.note: My role, as its README records it: SCRUM Master & Integration Lead. The README's success metrics are targets, not results.

outputs.title: EcoPrompt Coach — the maintained tool (promptcoach)
outputs.summary: A JavaScript engine, web app and Chrome extension that estimate the energy, water and carbon of an LLM prompt from published benchmarks, in everyday terms. Version 2's list of models runs to September 2026; the repo links the web app.
outputs.note: Began as a Digital Society School prototype. Its 2026 models are extrapolated, as no lab has published a figure for one; the extension runs unpacked, in no store.

outputs.title: EcoPrompt Coach — this site's edition, with its evidence ledger
outputs.summary: Interactive per-query footprint calculator, with an evidence ledger giving every emission factor a source, publication date, vintage, uncertainty range and review date. Input and output tokens are priced separately, because decode costs several times what prefill does.
outputs.note: Every factor is auditable from the page itself. Its code and data are its own, separate from the maintained tool's.

outputs.title: AI carbon factor set — sources, ranges and review dates
outputs.summary: The machine-readable factor set behind the EcoPrompt Coach and the homepage's AI energy chart: ten models, thirteen grid regions, four cooling profiles, plus PUE, the token-energy model and everyday equivalents — each with a citation, a vintage and a plausible range.
outputs.note: Reusable on its own. A test fails the build if any factor loses its source, range or review date.

outputs.title: Field Notes
outputs.summary: Short essays connecting the three threads: what 164 water points taught me about data, why I wrote a pessimistic future on purpose, and what to do about the footprint of a prompt.
outputs.note: Written for the site, not peer-reviewed.

outputs.title: Journey map generator — reproducible cartography
outputs.summary: Builds the site's journey map from Natural Earth 50 m coastlines: a region-fitted Natural Earth projection, variable simplification, and deterministic output. Pinned dependencies, and a check that the committed SVG still matches the script.
outputs.note: npm run map:build to regenerate, npm run map:check to verify. Byte-identical across runs.

reproducibility.heading: Reproducing what is here
reproducibility.body: The outputs that are part of this site run from its one clone, with no build step and no API key; each repository above says how to run it. The EcoPrompt Coach and the homepage's energy chart read one factor set, so they cannot disagree about a model. The chart shows each model's published figure for a 1,000-token answer; the coach multiplies it by data-centre overhead (PUE, 1.2 unless you change it), so for the same answer it prints 1.2 times the chart's figure. The map regenerates byte-identically from pinned dependencies. The narration is content-addressed, so re-rendering unchanged text costs nothing.
